title: Who told you your Lord was anything less than generous?
subtitle: The Generous and Noble One who gives without strings and honours His servants
intro: Al-Karim (الْكَرِيمُ) means the Most Generous and Noble, the One who gives abundantly without being asked, expects nothing in return, forgives with grace, and raises in honour whoever He wills. It is the name He uses when calling back those who have drifted far from Him.

root.sense: Karam joins two ideas: generosity and nobility. A karim person gives freely and gracefully, and is also honourable and of high worth. The Arabs called anything excellent of its kind karim. The Quran uses it for the Quran itself, for noble provision and for an honourable reward.

row.title: I am too far to come back
sub: He must be done with me

row.title: What deceived you about Him
sub: There is room for you still

knowing: Other names tell you how much Allah gives. {idea}Al-Karim tells you how He gives: freely, gracefully, without strings and without making you feel small.{/idea} People often give with expectations, out of guilt, or in a way that leaves the receiver humiliated. When Al-Karim gives, He expects nothing back, for He needs nothing. Sulayman said that whoever is ungrateful, his Lord is free of need and Karim (27:40).

Karam also means nobility. The Quran calls itself karim, and His reward and provision karim, meaning the best of their kind. He is the Most Noble, and He is the One who gives honour. He honoured all the children of Adam (17:70), and then raised among them whoever is most mindful of Him: the most noble of you in His sight is the most God-conscious (49:13).

His generosity reaches past giving into forgiving. Scholars describe the Karim as one who gives without being asked, forgives when he is able to punish, and keeps his word. {reward}The Prophet ﷺ said that your Lord is shy and generous, and is too shy to turn away empty the hands of a servant raised to Him{/reward} (Sunan Abi Dawud and Jami at-Tirmidhi).
seeing: In the very first revelation, the Prophet ﷺ was told twice to recite, and the second time with the words: your Lord is the Most Generous, Al-Akram, who taught by the pen (96:3). Before any commandment, he was introduced to a Lord whose generosity has no rival.

Al-Karim changed who counted. Bilal, once a slave whom society ignored, became a man whose footsteps the Prophet ﷺ heard ahead of him in Paradise, because of the two rakahs he prayed after every wudu (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim). {idea}Honour is His to give, and He gives it by a different scale than ours.{/idea}

Then there is the question He asks every human being: O mankind, what has deceived you about your Lord, Al-Karim, who created you, shaped you and balanced you (82:6-7)? He asks it of those who drifted, denied and forgot. Even in calling them to account, He reminds them first of His generosity.
trusting: If you feel you have gone too far, notice that this is exactly who Al-Karim addresses. {trap}Whoever convinced you that Allah is stingy with His forgiveness or quick to give up on you has deceived you about Him.{/trap} He created you without being asked; He will not refuse you when you finally ask.

Trust Him with your requests, and ask big. {reward}Hands raised to Al-Karim do not come back empty.{/reward} Ask in your own words, from the heart; He knows your language and your silences. And let His generosity loosen your own hand: give without reminding, without strings, without needing thanks.
loving: We love generous people, and love them more when they give without making us feel small. {reward}Al-Karim has given you life, body, mind and guidance, never once sent you a bill, and still calls you to more.{/reward} The heart cannot hold that and stay cold.
now: You have not prayed in months, and a friend asks if you are still Muslim. You laugh it off, but on the drive home you feel a door has closed. {idea}Al-Karim is asking you what deceived you about Him{/idea}. Pull over somewhere quiet, raise your hands, and tell Him in plain words that you want to come back.
old: After everything I have done, Allah must have given up on me.
new: Al-Karim gave to me before I ever asked; He will not turn me away now that I come asking.
try: Give something today without telling anyone and without wanting thanks: a meal, a gift, or paying for the person behind you.

dua.text: Ya Karim, You gave me everything before I asked. I did not ask You to create me or feed me, but I ask You now to guide me and honour me with nearness to You.
dua.note: Call on Him as Al-Karim when you feel unworthy to ask; His generosity is shy to send raised hands away empty.

pairs.why: Ghani Karim: He needs nothing from anyone, so His giving is pure generosity (27:40).
Al-Karim gives nobly; Al-Majeed is the vast glory in which that noble giving overflows.
Al-Karim gives with nobility and no strings; Al-Barr gives with gentle, faithful kindness.

faq.a: Al-Karim means the Most Generous and Noble. Karam combines generosity and honour: Allah gives abundantly without being asked and without expecting return, forgives when able to punish, keeps His promises, and is the highest in nobility, giving honour to whom He wills.

faq.q: What is the difference between Al-Karim and Al-Akram?
faq.a: Al-Akram, in 96:3, is the comparative form of the same root: the Most Generous, beyond anyone else's generosity. It appears in the first verses revealed to the Prophet ﷺ. Al-Karim is the name describing His generous, noble nature.

faq.q: Which verse asks what deceived you about Al-Karim?
faq.a: Surah Al-Infitar 82:6 asks: O mankind, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous? It then reminds the reader that He created, proportioned and balanced them, calling back those who have turned away with a reminder of His generosity.
